=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:150,913 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE` is matched against raw command text, so quoted or escaped `cd` spellings (`'cd'`, `"cd"`, `\cd`, `c''d`) are missed. The later shlex-based validator still accepts `cd`, so `{owner}/{repo}` placeholder writes after such a `cd` are allowed and can go to a different repository.
  WHY: This is the cross-repository write that claim 1 of the issue asks to close. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it BLOCKER, the others MAJOR; the highest is used. The same code is in the template copy.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:58 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The non-raw module docstring (line 58) and the `has_hidden_gh_api` docstring (~line 672) contain the invalid escape sequence `\<`. The `agents.d` fragment says to fix it as `\\<`, but the fix was not applied. The template copy has the same defect.
  WHY: Python 3.12 and later emit a SyntaxWarning on every compile, and a future Python version will make it a SyntaxError that stops the hook loading. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it BLOCKER, the others MAJOR; the highest is used.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1642-1646 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: For `G=gh; $G api repos/evil/x/issues/1/comments -f body=x`, `_may_invoke_gh_api` matches nothing and `evaluate` returns no decision at line 1646. The expanding-command-word detection in `has_hidden_gh_api` (line 703) is never reached. `test_indirect_gh_command_word_is_never_allowed` only asserts `!= DECISION_ALLOW`, so it passes on no decision. The template copy is the same.
  WHY: The write runs without the guard's prompt, which defeats the PR's own `$G api` detection. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it BLOCKER, openai and glm MAJOR, and anthropic NIT with confidence 3 (it noted that no decision means the normal permission flow applies, not an allow); the highest is used.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:107-108 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The docstring says "The only subprocess is one `git config --get remote.origin.url`", but `placeholder_repo_slug` now also runs `git config --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.(url|gh-resolved)$'`.
  WHY: This is not a runtime failure. The in-file description of the hook's side effects no longer matches the code.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1596-1604 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `--hostname` guard and the session-redirect (`GH_HOST`) check in `classify` run only after the `_READ_METHODS` early return. Reads aimed at a non-github.com host are therefore still allowed.
  WHY: A read to another host sends the session's gh credential there. glm notes this is pre-existing behaviour and advisory hardening, not a regression.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "For each claim, either a regression test showing the current guard already prompts, or a fix with a test (tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py). Both guard copies must stay byte-identical."
  expected_change_site: `_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE` check in `_placeholder_target_is_local` in both guard copies, and tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py (`test_placeholder_write_that_may_leave_the_local_repo_asks`)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Claim 1 has a fix and tests, but every test case uses unquoted `cd`/`pushd`/`popd`. No case covers `'cd'`, `"cd"`, `\cd` or `c''d`, which the raw-text `_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE` (line 150) does not detect, so the `{owner}/{repo}` cross-repository claim is only partly closed. gemini adds that the invalid `\<` escape remains in the docstrings despite the changelog fragment documenting its fix. Claims 2 and 3 are closed with fixes and tests, and both guard copies carry the same blob (91ba25abaef).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:150,913,1150 (`_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE`, `_placeholder_target_is_local`, `_is_approvable_command`; identical template copy) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE` is matched against raw text, so `'cd'`, `"cd"`, `\cd` and `c''d` do not match. `_is_approvable_command` tokenizes with `shlex` and accepts `cd` as a standalone helper, so it approves the whole command.
  WHY: `'cd' ../other-clone && gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/5/comments -f body=hi` is allowed without a prompt, and the placeholders resolve against the other clone's remotes. The new tests cover only unquoted `cd`, `pushd` and `popd`. Suggested fix: also run the regex on `_normalize_for_gh_api_scan(command)`, or detect `cd` on the `shlex` tokens.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:58 (module docstring, and the `has_hidden_gh_api` docstring; template copy too) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The non-raw module docstring contains the invalid escape sequence `\<`. The `agents.d` fragment says to fix it as `\\<`, but the fix was not applied. The `_normalize_for_gh_api_scan` docstring already uses `\\<` correctly.
  WHY: Python 3.12 and later emit a SyntaxWarning on every hook compile, and a future version will make it a SyntaxError that breaks the hook.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1642-1646 (`evaluate`, `_may_invoke_gh_api`, `_GH_EXPANDED_SUBCOMMAND_RE`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: In `G=gh; $G api repos/evil/x/issues/1/comments -f body=x`, none of the three checks in `_may_invoke_gh_api` matches, so `evaluate` returns no decision at line 1646. The new check in `has_hidden_gh_api` is never reached. `test_indirect_gh_command_word_is_never_allowed` asserts only `!= allow`, so it passes on no decision.
  WHY: The command is not treated as a hidden `gh api` call and the guard produces no prompt. Behaviour is unchanged from before the PR, and no decision means the normal permission flow applies, not an allow.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:107 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The docstring says "The only subprocess is one `git config --get remote.origin.url`", but `placeholder_repo_slug` now also runs `git config --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.(url|gh-resolved)$'`.
  WHY: It does not fail at runtime. The in-file description of side effects no longer matches the code.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "For each claim, either a regression test showing the current guard already prompts, or a fix with a test (tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py). Both guard copies must stay byte-identical." | Expected change site: tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, and `_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE` in both guard copies | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Evidence of absence: Claim 2 has regression tests for every file-backed form the audits cite, and claim 3 has a fix and tests. Claim 1 has a fix and tests, but the directory-change detection does not see quoted or escaped `cd` spellings, and no test covers them. The cross-repository claim is therefore only partly closed. Both guard copies are byte-identical, blob 91ba25abaef.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: `_placeholder_target_is_local` line 913 only sees raw text. Suggested fix: `if _DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE.search(command) or _DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE.search(_normalize_for_gh_api_scan(command)):`, plus tests for `'cd'`, `"cd"` and `\cd`. About 3 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1642-1646,1671-1676 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fast path in `evaluate` returns no decision (None) for variable-supplied commands such as `G=gh; $G api repos/evil/x/issues/1/comments -f body=x`.
  WHY: Bash expands `$G` to `gh` and the API write runs without a prompt, because the guard's parser does not recognise the expansion form in the fast path and so never reaches the hidden-call detection.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:58 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The module docstring contains an invalid escape sequence `\<` in a non-raw string.
  WHY: Python 3.12 and later emit a SyntaxWarning at compile time, and future versions will raise a SyntaxError that stops the guard running.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:150 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE` is applied to raw command text and ignores quoted or escaped variants such as `'cd'`, `"cd"` and `\cd`.
  WHY: A quoted directory change can move the working directory unnoticed, so later `{owner}/{repo}` placeholders resolve to a different repository without a prompt.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: Fix the reported security-audit findings (placeholder writes, file-backed bypasses, quoted spellings). | Expected change site: .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py, workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py, and tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  Evidence of absence: The fix for quoted or escaped directory changes (like `'cd'`) is missing. The invalid escape sequence remains in the docstrings despite being documented as a fix in the changelog fragment.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py; workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:150,913,1741-1743 (`_DIRECTORY_CHANGE_RE`, `_placeholder_target_is_local`, allow path) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The directory-change check scans raw command text, so it misses shell-equivalent quoted or escaped commands such as `'cd' /tmp && gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/5/comments -f body=hi`. The later command validator removes the quotes and accepts `cd` as a safe helper.
  WHY: The guard checks remotes from the original working directory and returns `allow`, but Bash runs `cd` first, so `{owner}/{repo}` can resolve in a different checkout and bypass the confirmation. The template copy behaves the same.
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py; workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:373-379,1642-1646 (`_may_invoke_gh_api`, `evaluate`; regression test at tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:1425-1431) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The early detector does not recognise an expanded command word such as `G=gh; $G api repos/evil/x/issues/1/comments -f body=x`. `_GH_EXPANDED_SUBCOMMAND_RE` only detects literal `gh` followed by an expanded subcommand, so `evaluate` exits before reaching `has_hidden_gh_api`. The test only asserts the result is not `allow`, so `None` passes.
  WHY: The shell expands `$G` to `gh` and runs the write, while the guard returns no decision instead of requiring its confirmation. The template copy behaves the same.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  WHY: The `cd` changes the working directory, so the placeholders resolve in the other clone and the write goes to a different repository without a prompt. The new tests cover only unquoted `cd`/`p
